title: Bare-Metal Host VM Revenue Maximization
real_world_story: A cloud infrastructure provider is commissioning a flagship bare-metal physical server equipped with M gigabytes of total RAM. N enterprise client virtual machines (VMs) are requesting placement on this server. VM i requires m_i GB of RAM and yields an agreed monthly rental revenue of p_i dollars. Due to hypervisor isolation constraints, each VM must reside entirely on a single host—VMs cannot be split or shared. Determine the maximum total monthly revenue achievable on this host without exceeding memory capacity M.
problem_statement: Given total RAM capacity M and N virtual machines, where VM i requires memory m_i and yields revenue p_i, determine the maximum total revenue achievable by selecting a subset of VMs such that the total memory does not exceed M. Each VM can be selected at most once.
task: Compute the maximum monthly revenue achievable within the host RAM capacity M.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and M, the number of VMs and the host RAM capacity in GB.
The next N lines each contain two space-separated integers m_i and p_i, the RAM requirement and revenue of the i-th VM.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum monthly revenue.

examples.explanation: Selecting VM 2 (32 GB, 120) and VM 3 (32 GB, 110) consumes 32 + 32 = 64 GB <= 64 GB and yields revenue 120 + 110 = 230. This exceeds selecting VM 1 + VM 2 (16 + 32 = 48 GB, revenue 170). Maximum revenue is 230.
Both VMs exceed the host memory capacity of 32 GB. Total revenue is 0.

real_world_takeaway: 0/1 Knapsack optimization allows cloud providers to maximize revenue yield per physical host while enforcing strict virtualization capacity limits.
